title: Addiction and Bondage
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Addiction and bondage describes the enslaving power of sinful desires, habits, substances, behaviors, or patterns that master a person and distort life before God. Addiction is not solved by shame or willpower alone; people need truth, repentance, grace, deliverance, discipleship, and hope in Christ.

christFocus: Jesus Christ came to set captives free. Through His death and resurrection, He forgives guilt, breaks sin’s dominion, gives new life, and leads bound people into freedom under His gracious lordship.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Addiction reveals how deeply bondage can affect human life. A person may hate the consequences of a pattern and still feel pulled back into it. Sin promises relief, escape, control, pleasure, or comfort, but often produces slavery, shame, damage, secrecy, and despair.

Scripture teaches that sin can master people. This does not remove personal responsibility, but it does show that bondage is deeper than bad decisions alone. People need more than advice, embarrassment, punishment, or temporary motivation. They need deliverance through Christ and a new way of life.

The Gospel gives real hope for the addicted and bound. Christ forgives sinners, breaks the dominion of sin, gives new identity, and brings people into the freedom of belonging to Him. Freedom does not mean the battle is always quick or easy, but it means bondage does not have the final word.

Recovery must become discipleship. True restoration is not merely stopping a destructive behavior; it is learning to walk with Christ, live in truth, confess honestly, receive grace, repair what can be repaired, and grow in holiness with the help of God’s Word, Spirit, and people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people trapped in addiction are buried under shame. Others excuse bondage as though change is impossible. Some churches treat addiction only as scandal, while the world may treat it only as sickness without addressing sin, worship, repentance, and spiritual freedom. Scripture gives a fuller answer.

This doctrine tells the truth without removing hope. Addiction is serious, destructive, and enslaving, but Christ is stronger. The bound person is not helped by denial or condemnation alone. He needs the Gospel, honest repentance, wise support, Spirit-empowered change, and patient discipleship.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring bondage into the light before God and trusted help. Do not hide, excuse, or make peace with what is destroying you. Confess honestly, turn to Christ, remove what feeds the bondage, seek faithful accountability, and walk one day at a time in grace. If you are helping someone in addiction, speak truth without cruelty, offer hope without minimizing sin, and keep pointing them to Christ-centered recovery and discipleship.
